title: SchemaRenderer node visibleWhen still fails open on a fault; page:tabs items now fail closed
body:
Filing gate: **① a user-visible defect at a named site** (`pm:queue` class), with an open direction question for triage. Filed by `domain:ui` seat 2 (`session_01XVp19E1MYUTFM3dnkwz8gB`) from the os-dev report on PR #13297 (objectui#13286). ⛔ Not a claim.

**Reader (who acts):** triage first (route: queue, or `needs-user-decision` if the fail direction of the node gate is a product call); then the objectui `domain:ui` lane.

## What

objectui#13286 (PR #13297) makes a `page:tabs` item `visibleWhen` that faults on evaluation (over the CEL AST bound, a type error, an unbound root, a missing function) **withhold** its tab. The node-level gate in `packages/react/src/SchemaRenderer.tsx` (`visibleWhen` / `visible` / `visibleOn` on any page node) still answers the same fault with `evaluateCondition`'s fail-soft `true`. A stored page whose block `visibleWhen` faults therefore still draws that block for a viewer the predicate was written to exclude. The fault is reported once, in both builds (objectui#6038, objectui#6503). The SchemaRenderer docblock (near the `onFault` production branch) says the fail-open semantics were "not its to move", which leaves the flip to a card of its own. This is that card.

The `page:tabs` count-probe gates in `packages/components/src/renderers/layout/containers.tsx` (`isGateOpen`) mirror the node gate so a tab's badge counts what is drawn. They move with whichever way the node gate goes.

`content/docs/guide/metadata-diagnostics.md` now documents the split: one gate in the family fails closed, the rest fail open.

**Options (from the dev report, not a ruling):**
- **A:** flip the node visibility legs to fail closed (hidden on a fault), with the count-probe gates in the same PR. Cost: a shipped behaviour change on every page node; the existing fail-open pins in `packages/react` flip; medium effort. The dev recommends A: the measured case (a stored over-budget predicate) faults the same way on a block as on a tab, and one fault direction for every page visibility gate removes the split the docs now describe.
- **B:** keep the node gate fail-soft as documented and treat the tab-item gate as the only fail-closed page visibility gate. Zero effort; the block keeps drawing for an excluded viewer.

Out of scope either way: form field rules (`visibleWhen` / `readonlyWhen` on fields) keep their documented fail-open (objectui#13286 ruling 3).

class: a · reach: any stored page whose block-level `visibleWhen` faults, shown to every viewer the predicate meant to exclude.
Dedupe words: SchemaRenderer visibleWhen fail closed, node visibility fault fail-open, page block visibleWhen over budget shown. Parent: objectui#13286. No other open card covers it.
